answer: A reputation bond works like a summit every agent must climb before earning trust: newcomers post a refundable stake that is slashed if they are caught running duplicate identities. Honest agents recover the stake plus fees, so the terrace of verified participants stays small and accountable, while a Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity separately and loses every bond when the fraud is detected. The system is no oasis for free riders — creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds, which makes large-scale fakery unprofitable by design.
